Subject: Quick ask — per-1M IO pricing and hosted model roster

Hi Marissa,

We're evaluating vendors for the backend LLM layer for a clinician-facing assistant at ApexCare. Can you send the standard hosted API IO rate (per 1M tokens) split by input vs output, and a short list of the models you host today (and which are recommended for low-latency real-time chat vs high-quality long-form generation)?

A few context points:
- Launch target: pilot with ~10M tokens/month, expected growth to ~50M over 6–12 months.
- Latency expectation: sub-300ms p95 for short chat responses would be ideal.
- We're also curious about committed-volume discounts (12-month) and whether embeddings are billed differently.

No need for a full contract yet — a baseline ratecard and a one-page model roster will help our procurement/engineering sync.

Thanks,
Nora
Nora Patel
Head of Product, ApexCare

Subject: Re: Quick ask — per-1M IO pricing and hosted model roster

Hi Nora — thanks for the context and the clear ask. Attached is our baseline hosted ratecard snapshot and a short model roster. Summary below to get you moving quickly:

Baseline hosted IO pricing (standard, no commitment) 
- Input tokens: $0.40 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $0.90 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings: $1.20 per 1M embedding-units (separate meter)

Recommended models (hosted API) — quick guidance:
- rwd-base-7b (low-latency chat): best for sub-300ms p95, suitable for interactive assistants where cost matters
- rwd-legacy-13b (balanced): better quality for multi-turn context, moderate latency
- rwd-xl-70b (high-quality long-form): highest quality, expect higher p95 and cost; good for summarization and document generation
- community-quant (quantized option): lower-cost variant for batch workloads, not recommended for strict latency SLOs

Notes on discounts & commitments:
- Standard committed-volume tiers (12-month) — ranges we frequently offer: 10% off @ 200M tokens, 18% off @ 500M tokens, custom pricing above that. These are illustrative; legal and finance will sign off on final tiers for a term.
- We can split IO differently for packaging (e.g., subscription + overages) if you prefer predictable spend.

Latency and SLA options:
- Hosted API has best-effort latency; we publish per-model p95 profiles in the catalog.
- If you need guaranteed SLOs, Dedicated or Private deployments are the route (we can include that in an enterprise proposal).

I've attached a short PDF (Redwood_Hosted_Baseline_Ratecard_Q3_2027.pdf) with the above numbers and an expanded model compatibility table. A couple quick questions back to you:
- For the pilot, do you expect chat traffic to be dominated by short queries (<=64 tokens response) or longer generations?
- Would you want embeddings bundled with your token commit or treated separately?

If helpful, I can set up a 30-minute call this week with Ben (sales lead) and one of our solutions engineers to walk through performance profiles and cost modeling.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the fast reply and the PDF. A few follow-ups inline: 

> For the pilot, do you expect chat traffic to be dominated by short queries (<=64 tokens response) or longer generations?
We expect 75% short replies (20–80 output tokens) and 25% longer (200–800 tokens) for follow-ups and note drafting.

> Would you want embeddings bundled with your token commit or treated separately?
We'd prefer embeddings treated separately for now, but we'll probably bundle them later if the cost profile makes sense.

A couple more items from procurement:
- Can you confirm whether input vs output measurement strips punctuation / client-side whitespace the same way across models? We need consistent metering for forecasting.
- For the committed tiers you mentioned, does the discount apply to both input and output IO lines equally?

We are targeting a vendor decision by end of month, and a 30-minute call with Ben + SE would be helpful. Available windows: Thu 09/16 10–11am PT or Fri 09/17 1–3pm PT.

Thanks — Nora
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Nora — great, thanks for the clarifications. Quick answers: 
- Metering: we strip leading/trailing whitespace consistently and use tokenization rules based on the model family; input/output metering is consistent across hosted models (we'll include the exact tokenizer spec in the follow-up SE doc).
- Discounts: yes — committed discounts are applied to both input & output IO lines unless you request an alternate structure (e.g., lower discount on embeddings).

Proposed next step: booked a 30-minute sync for Fri 09/17 at 1:30pm PT with Ben and our senior SE. Agenda: 1) performance profile per model for your token mix, 2) discount modeling for a 12-month commit at 200M vs 500M tokens, 3) brief runbook for Dedicated/Private options.

If anything changes on your side, let me know. Otherwise we'll send a calendar invite and the SE performance notes before the call.
